text: Well, Larry, it makes me sick to my stomach, but it doesn't surprise me one bit. We've known from day one that he is a liar. He lied to us, he lied to the authorities, and he led us on a wild-goose chase about where he left my daughter. For months, we've had to sit here and watch him change his story over and over again while Natalee is still missing. Every time he opens his mouth, it’s just another manipulation. But no matter what he says on television or how much he tries to spin it, the truth is going to come out. I will not stop, and I will stay here as long as it takes until we get the answers and accountability we deserve.

It makes me sick to my stomach, Larry. To sit there and watch him lie again, just like he has since day one. He is a murderer, and he knows exactly what happened to Natalee. He and those two Surinamese brothers took my daughter's life, and he has lied and manipulated ever since to cover it up. For him to sit there and try to play the victim or act like he's innocent is just pure evil. We have known the truth all along, and I am not going to stop until there is full accountability and justice for Natalee.

It makes me sick to my stomach, honestly. After all these years of lies, manipulation, and playing games with my family's emotions, watching him sit there and try to play the victim is just despicable. He has never shown an ounce of genuine remorse, and today is no different. He knows exactly what he did to Natalee, and he knows he's cornered now, so he resorts to the same old tactics. But no amount of whining or false pleading on television is going to change the facts or hide the evil that he is. We just want justice, and we want him to finally be held fully accountable for what he stole from us.

It sickens me to my stomach, Beth. To watch him sit there and look so calm, trying to spin this web of lies and play the victim, is just infuriating. We are talking about a young woman’s life that was so brutally stolen, and all he cares about is saving his own skin. He has lied from day one, changing his story over and over again whenever the pressure gets to be too much. Seeing him on that screen, showing zero remorse, just proves what a manipulative psychopath he really is. He thinks he can outsmart everyone, but the truth is going to catch up to him. He belongs behind bars, and he needs to finally take responsibility for what he did to Natalee.

Well, it's just breathtaking, isn't it? Because you see someone who is so entirely disconnected from the reality of their own actions. We always want to believe that if someone is confronted with something so serious, there will be some sort of visible crack in the facade, some moment of profound reckoning where they finally tell the truth. But people like that—they have their own script. They are entirely invested in a narrative where they are the victim, and they will just keep repeating it no matter how absurd it sounds to the rest of the world. It’s a masterclass in denial, and honestly, it’s chilling to watch someone look right into the camera and expect everyone else to buy into a version of events that defies all logic and decency.

That is completely absurd and just another lie in a long string of lies. From the very beginning, Joran has changed his story over and over again. First it was that he dropped her off at the Holiday Inn, then it was something else, and now this. You cannot believe a single word that comes out of his mouth. He is trying to protect himself and cover up what really happened that night. We know the truth, and we are not going to stop until we get full accountability and answers. I’ve kept a journal since day one, and the timeline, the evidence, and their deceit all point to the fact that they know exactly what happened to Natalee. We will keep fighting for the truth, no matter how many lies he tells.

That is absolute garbage. It’s just another lie in a long string of lies that he has told since day one. He lied to us on the very morning Natalee went missing, telling us he dropped her off at the hotel, and he has changed his story every single time the pressure gets turned up on him. We know what kind of person he is, and we know he is completely incapable of telling the truth. After all this time, he’s still trying to protect himself and play games, but nobody believes a word coming out of his mouth. We are here for the truth, and we are not going to stop until we have answers and accountability for what happened to my daughter.

I don't believe a single word of it. It makes no sense at all. He spends hours with my daughter, concocts this bizarre story about a condom, and expects everyone to just accept that he walked away and left her alone on a dark beach? That is not what a normal, innocent person does. No parent could ever buy an excuse like that. My daughter trusted people, and now she’s gone, and this man is sitting there making up convenient alibis to save his own skin. I want the truth, and I want true accountability for what was done to her, because nothing about his version of events adds up.

It just doesn't make any sense. My daughter is gone, and this man is giving a story that changes by the minute, full of holes and excuses. You don't just leave a young woman alone on a dark beach in the middle of the night. No parent can accept that kind of explanation. We are searching for the truth, and we want accountability for what was done to her. Every day is an agonizing wait for answers, and we are not going to stop until we know exactly what happened out there.

Oh, my God. That is just devastating to hear, and it makes me sick to my stomach. Look, when you're in a situation that is that terrifying and out of your control, your mind immediately goes to the worst possible place. But right now, we can't get bogged down trying to write the script for what he should have done or demanding answers he might not be capable of giving. We have to focus on the reality of the situation and do everything in our power to find her. It's completely unnatural and heartbreaking, and I wouldn't wish this kind of agony on any parent. We just have to keep moving forward, use every common sense strategy we have, and pray we get her back safely.

I think you go through every possible scenario in your mind, especially when you've been searching for answers for as long as I have. At the beginning, you hold onto the hope that she's out there being held somewhere, and that's why we pushed so hard with the rewards and the searches. But as time goes on and you look at the total lack of cooperation from the people who were last with her—Joran and the others—you realize the grim reality. They lied to us from day one. I believe in my heart that she didn't survive that night, and that those young men know exactly what happened to her and where she is. That is what we are still fighting to uncover, the absolute truth, so we can finally bring her home.

I have lived every nightmare imaginable since Natalee disappeared, and through all the agonizing weeks and months on that island and the years since, you search for any piece of truth. At this point, with everything we have faced and all the investigations, I believe deep down that she was killed that very night. They took her life, and then they disposed of her body to ensure she would never be found. It is the most horrific realization a parent can come to, but when you look at how those individuals acted, the lies they told from the very beginning, and the lengths they went to cover it up, that is the grim reality I have had to face. We are still searching for finality, but that belief is what drives me to keep fighting for justice every single day.

I think about it every single day, and honestly, the theories change depending on the hour, depending on what the wind sounds like outside. Some days I lean toward the idea that she just wanted to walk away, to start completely over somewhere where nobody knew her name or expected anything of her. She was hurting, and young people sometimes think running is the only cure. But other days, the silence goes on too long, and my heart tells me something darker happened. Someone took advantage of her kindness, her trust. That is the one I try not to look at, because if I really let myself believe that, I don't know how I would get out of bed. I am just not sure anymore. I just want the truth, whatever it is, so I can finally breathe.

I really don't have just one fixed theory, and that is the hardest part of living through this every single day. You go through every possible scenario in your mind. You replay the timeline, you look at the evidence, and one day you think one thing, and the next day something else makes more sense. The not knowing is what truly tortures a family. I just want the truth, whatever it may be, so we can finally bring her home and have some measure of peace. Until that day comes, we are left in this terrible limbo, searching for answers and hoping that someone out there knows something and finally finds the courage to come forward.

You know, I don't think you ever really get the luxury of just having one neat theory, because your mind goes to a million different places, especially when you're dealing with something so devastating and so bewildering. You cycle through hope and despair and every possible scenario you can dream up. But the hardest part is that you can't write the script for how this ends, no matter how desperately you want to. You're just left trying to survive the not knowing, and it's the kind of heartbreak where you learn pretty quickly that holding out for specific answers or the exact words you need to hear just isn't going to happen. You have to find a way to live in the uncertainty, as impossible as that feels most days.

I do. I believe that he is responsible for her death, and that he disposed of her body. From the very beginning, when he and the others lied to us about where they dropped her off and what happened that night, we knew they were hiding something terrible. We have lived through an absolute nightmare for years, searching for answers, and every piece of information that has come to light only reinforces what we have felt in our hearts all along. We are looking for justice for Natalee, and we will not stop until the truth is fully exposed and she is finally brought home.

I believe that every single piece of evidence, everything we have fought to uncover over all these years, points directly to Joran van der Sloot. He lied from the very first night, he manipulated everyone, and he has never shown an ounce of remorse. When you look at the totality of what happened, how he targeted Natalee, how he deceived us, and the absolute lack of any other credible explanation, there is no doubt in my mind that he is responsible for her disappearance and her death. We have sought truth and accountability every single day since she vanished, and we will not stop until justice is fully served for Natalee.

I do. From the very beginning, every piece of evidence, every lie told, and every action points to the fact that he is responsible for what happened to my daughter. He destroyed our lives, and he has never shown an ounce of remorse. Filing this lawsuit wasn't just about holding him accountable financially; it is about finding the truth and getting justice for my child. No parent should ever have to go through the nightmare we have endured, and I will not stop fighting until the full truth comes to light and he pays for what he did.

I truly believe he did. Everything that we have uncovered, and everything we have felt in our hearts since our daughter disappeared, points directly to him. When you look at the pattern of behavior, the lies, and the complete lack of remorse, it is impossible for us to reach any other conclusion. He took her away from us, and he has hidden the truth for years. We didn't take this step lightly by filing this lawsuit, but we are desperate for accountability and desperate to finally find out where our daughter is. We want the truth to come out, and we want justice for what he did to her.

I don't know the exact words to use, and I'm not here to write a script for anyone else, but I can tell you how devastated and heartbroken I am. When you've experienced the kind of profound loss and pain that comes with something like this, you don't chase after hollow apologies from someone who isn't capable of offering them. You just have to be radically, deeply honest about your truth and the reality of what happened. I've learned in my own life that you can't force the other person to step up or give you what you need, but you can stand up for yourself and refuse to let silence become complicity. My focus has simply been on facing this with as much honesty and courage as I possibly can.

Well, Larry, I can tell you that my feelings have certainly not gotten better over time. In fact, if anything, they have only grown more frustrating because of the complete lack of transparency and action from the very beginning. From the first 48 hours when we were sitting in a car waiting for search warrants that weren't being issued, to the months of watching authorities allow people to lie and obstruct justice without real consequences, it has been an uphill battle every single step of the way. We had to push for everything ourselves, utilizing private investigators and relying on the incredible support of friends and family just to keep any momentum going. While we remain entirely focused on getting answers and finding out what happened to Natalee, the handling of this case by the local officials has left us with far more questions than answers.

Well, Larry, my feelings haven't gotten better over time, because from day one, we watched them waste precious hours and days when they should have been securing evidence, impounding cars, and thoroughly questioning those suspects. Instead, they allowed lies to go unchallenged and didn't take the aggressive action that was required immediately following Natalee's disappearance. Even now, looking back, the frustration remains because we are still searching for answers that should have been uncovered at the very beginning if the authorities had handled this investigation with the urgency and seriousness it demanded. Our relationship with them was strained from the start, and unfortunately, that lack of trust has not changed.

My feelings have unfortunately only grown worse over time because of the sheer lack of transparency and communication from the start. In the beginning, we gave them the benefit of the doubt, hoping they were doing everything possible to find out what happened and bring Natalee home. But as the days turned into weeks and months, it became glaringly obvious that they were mishandling critical evidence and ignoring vital leads. My relationship with them right now is practically nonexistent, because they have frozen us out and refused to share meaningful updates. As for where the investigation stands, it feels completely stalled, which is agonizing for our family. We are still sitting here, after all this time, desperate for answers and accountability, while it feels like they have simply swept the whole tragedy under the rug.

Well, I can tell you that my feelings haven't really improved, because we still don't have answers. Early on, there was a terrible lack of communication and urgency from the Aruban authorities, and unfortunately, that pattern has largely continued. Every time we think there might be some momentum or a genuine effort being made, we hit another wall of silence. My relationship with them at this point is practically non-existent because they simply are not sharing information with us. As for where the investigation stands, as far as a grieving family is concerned, it feels like it is completely stalled. We are no closer to finding out what truly happened than we were in the very beginning, and that is a devastating reality to live with every single day.

Well, you know, I think that early on, emotions were just running so high, and when you are in the middle of a parent's worst nightmare, your patience is non-existent. You want answers immediately, and you want everyone working with the exact same sense of urgency that you feel in your chest every single second of the day. Over time, I’ve had to learn that you can't just bully or demand your way through an international investigation. It’s challenging, and it requires a kind of diplomacy that doesn't come naturally when your child is missing. I’ve tried to focus less on pointing fingers and more on keeping the lines of communication open, because at the end of the day, we all need to be pulling in the exact same direction to find out what happened.

When I watch that, my mind immediately goes back to those endless, agonizing weeks on the island, holding onto every shred of hope, waiting for someone to finally tell the truth. Every single day was a battle to keep things moving forward, to push the authorities, and to ensure my daughter wasn't forgotten. It brings back the raw pain of that uncertainty, but also the overwhelming gratitude I still feel for the incredible supporters who stood by our side every step of the way. We were desperate for answers, and I would have done anything, gone anywhere, and pushed every possible boundary to find out what happened to Natalee.

When I watch that and think back to those agonizing weeks in Aruba, my mind just goes right back to the sheer exhaustion, but also the relentless determination that kept me going. Every single day was a battle to keep Natalee's name out there, to keep any possible lead alive, and to push authorities when we felt like we were hitting brick walls. You live in this surreal nightmare where you're holding onto any thread of hope—whether it's an increased reward, a new tip, or the support of incredible people standing by our side. It brings back the heavy burden of not knowing, but it also reminds me of why I never stopped fighting and why I said I would stay there until I found her.

When I see that footage, I just feel a deep sense of frustration mixed with resolve. For months, working families have been waiting for leadership in Washington to take real action on the cost of living, and instead, we keep seeing the same political games and excuses. People are sitting at their kitchen tables trying to figure out how to afford groceries and gas, while millions are being spent on endless gridlock. We need to stop the finger-pointing and actually deliver results for the people who sent us there. That is what goes through my mind, because the time for talk ran out a long time ago.

Well, Beth, when I see that, my mind goes right back to the grit and the grind of it all. You're looking at folks who aren't just doing a job; they're holding up a whole way of life, come hell or high water. It makes you proud, but it also makes you worry, because the folks down in Washington just don't understand what it takes to pull a living out of the ground day in and day out. They sit in their air-conditioned offices passing rules, while people out here are sweating and bleeding just to keep the lights on and the food on America's tables. So mostly, I just feel a deep respect for our people, and a hope that somebody finally starts listening to them before it's too late.

Well, when I watch that, I think about how much we all struggle to connect with the people we love, even when it feels completely impossible. We go into these family gatherings carrying all our old scripts and expectations, and we just brace ourselves for the worst. But human relationships are so wonderfully messy. Even when things are awkward or complicated—whether it's dealing with a tricky stepmother, a relative glued to a smartphone, or just trying to navigate your own place in the family—there's always room for a little bit of grace and common sense. We try so hard to force things to be a certain way, when really, the best moments happen when we let go of the need for perfection, find a neutral topic, or maybe even use a child as a human shield just to get through Christmas dinner.

Larry, absolutely not. I do not believe they are being truthful at all. They have lied to us from the very beginning, starting with the claim that they dropped Natalee off at the Holiday Inn. We know that was a complete fabrication. They were with her, they know what happened to my daughter, and they are covering it up. Day in and day out, they have protected each other and held back the truth while I have sat here on this island searching for answers. If they truly had nothing to hide, they would have been honest with the authorities from day one instead of engaging in deception. I am praying that their conscience or the mounting evidence finally breaks through so we can find out what they did to Natalee and where she is.

I don't believe for a second that they're being truthful. From the very beginning, they lied to us. They looked us in the eye and told us they dropped Natalee off at the Holiday Inn, and we now know that was a complete fabrication. They were with her, they know what happened that night, and they have protected each other instead of doing the right thing. If they truly had nothing to hide, why wouldn't they cooperate fully with the authorities from day one? Instead, we've faced roadblocks, silence, and deception. I keep a journal, and the list of things they and Joran have hidden and lied about just goes on and on. They played a role in this, and they know where Natalee is.

Well, Greta, my clients have maintained from the very beginning, through multiple extensive interrogations and searches by the authorities here in Aruba, that they have told the complete truth about everything they know. They cooperated fully with the police, they turned over their electronic devices, and they answered every question put to them without hesitation. There is simply no evidence connecting them to any wrongdoing in the disappearance of Natalee Holloway. It is easy for people abroad to speculate and point fingers, but the reality is that the investigators here have thoroughly vetted their statements and found no reason to detain or charge them. They want closure just as much as anyone, but continuing to cast suspicion on individuals who have been thoroughly investigated and cleared by the facts does not help find the truth.

Well, based on everything I have seen and the information that has come to light regarding this investigation, I believe the Kalpoe brothers know a lot more than they are currently sharing. Their stories have shifted, and their initial reluctance to cooperate fully raises serious red flags. When you look at the timeline of that night and their proximity to Natalee Holloway, it is difficult to accept that they were merely bystanders who dropped her off and simply walked away without a backward glance. I think they hold vital information about what happened to Natalee, and the pressure needs to remain on them until they decide to tell the complete truth and give this family the closure we desperately need.

Well, you know, it is so hard to look at a situation like this from the outside and know what's really in someone's heart or what they're hiding. When people are facing something this massive and terrifying, the instinct to circle the wagons and protect yourself can be overwhelming, even if it means staying quiet when you should speak up. But I always think about how truth has a way of coming out eventually, and carrying the weight of a secret like that must be an incredible burden. Sometimes, instead of trying to script what people *should* do, you have to look at the reality of human behavior—when someone is deep in self-preservation mode, they aren't always capable of doing the right thing right away. It's just devastating for the families waiting for answers.

It is the most excruciating thing a mother can ever experience. Every single day is a battle. You wake up, and for a split second, you forget, and then reality crashes down on you all over again. Not knowing is a kind of torture that I wouldn't wish on my worst enemy. But I have to keep going. I have to be her voice, because Natalee cannot speak for herself right now. We are still here, we are still searching, and we will not stop until we have the answers and until Natalee is brought home. The support we’ve received from people all over has been incredible, and that, along with my faith, is what keeps me standing, day after agonizing day.

It is an absolute nightmare that no parent should ever have to live through. Every single day is a struggle just to put one foot in front of the other. You wake up and for a brief second you forget, and then the reality crashes down all over again. Not knowing where she is or what happened to her is a form of torture, but what keeps me going is the fierce determination to find the truth. I promised Natalee that I would stay here and I would do everything in my power to bring her home, and I am not going to stop. We need answers, and we will not rest until we have them.

It is a kind of torture that doesn't ever really stop. Every morning when I wake up, for a split second, I forget, and then it crashes all over me again like a physical blow. Not knowing is the hardest part of it all. If there was an end, if we had answers, as painful as they might be, we could at least begin to find some ground to stand on. But this limbo, this endless searching and wondering where she is, if she’s warm, if she’s safe, it drains the life right out of you. You just keep going because you have to, because she deserves for us to keep fighting, but inside, every single day is a battle just to breathe.

It is the hardest thing in the world to wake up every single day and not know where my little girl is or who took her from us. Every time the phone rings, my heart stops, praying it is finally some news, any news, that brings her back home. You just try to keep putting one foot in front of the other for the sake of our family, but the not knowing is a torture that never lets up. We just want answers, and we want our daughter back where she belongs.

Well, it is the kind of heartbreak that is almost impossible to describe in words, because it's like a physical ache that never really goes away. But I've learned that you have to find a way to keep moving forward, even when the not knowing is so agonizing. You try to focus on the love you share and the memories, and you just take it one single day at a time, because looking at the whole mountain is simply too much to bear.

It's just infuriating. You sit there and you listen to him, and it's the exact same pattern of lies and manipulation that we've been dealing with since day one back in Aruba. He changes his story depending on who he's talking to and what he thinks they want to hear, never taking any real responsibility or telling the absolute truth about what happened to Natalee. After all these years, to still have to sit and watch him play these games—it's sickening. But I've never stopped fighting for answers, and I never will, because Natalee deserves justice, and the truth is going to come out no matter how hard he tries to spin it.

It makes me sick to my stomach, Larry. To sit here and listen to him lie over and over again, just like he has from the very beginning. He has never told the truth about what happened to Natalee. He manipulated us, he lied to our faces when we were searching for her in Aruba, and he’s still doing it today. He thinks he can go on television and play games with people's lives, but we see right through him. After all these years, he still refuses to take responsibility or give us the one thing we’ve been desperate for since day one: answers. We are never going to stop fighting for justice, and we are never going to let the world forget what he did.

Well, I think what we are seeing is a very carefully calculated performance designed to deflect responsibility away from himself and onto anyone else he can implicate. Having watched him closely for a very long time, this pattern is completely consistent with how he operates when the pressure mounts. He speaks in absolutes, he attempts to rewrite the narrative in real time, and he relies on the assumption that the public will confuse volume with innocence. But the facts of the matter do not change simply because he goes on television to rebrand them. We are talking about serious institutional failures and accountability, and no amount of television interviews is going to erase the record that investigators and journalists have painstakingly put together.

Well, what we are seeing here is a very carefully orchestrated performance designed to deflect accountability away from the central figure. When you look at the track record and the sheer volume of credible accounts spanning decades, this sudden pivot to total innocence simply does not align with the reality of the situation. It is frustrating, though unfortunately not surprising, to watch someone with that level of institutional protection use a national platform to rewrite the narrative. The public deserves transparency and honesty, not a sanitized version of events meant to manage public relations rather than face the truth of what actually occurred.

Well, it’s just fascinating to watch because it’s such a classic human reaction when someone is cornered. They want to rewrite the script entirely. They’re looking for a way out without having to utter the words that actually acknowledge what they’ve done. But the rest of us are sitting here watching the actions, not just listening to the PR-crafted statements, and you can't unsee how someone behaves when the pressure is on. It reminds me of why demanding a specific apology from someone who isn't capable of giving it is usually a dead end. Instead, you just have to look at the reality of how they handle themselves, take note, and draw your own conclusions about who they are.

You know, I don't see it as prolonging anything. Every step we take, every action we push for, is about one thing and one thing only: finding the truth about what happened to Natalee. We have kept a journal since day one, and from the very beginning, we’ve had to fight to get things moving, to get answers, and to hold people accountable. Filing this isn't about raising false hopes; it's about exhausting every possible avenue to get justice and to find our daughter. We will never stop searching, and we will never stop asking questions until we know where Natalee is and what happened to her.

No, I don't worry about that at all. In fact, filing this lawsuit is just another way of keeping things moving forward and fighting for the truth. For months and years, we have dealt with silence, lies, and a complete lack of accountability. If the authorities and the legal system aren't going to get answers, then we have to use every tool available to us to find out what happened to Natalee. We have never stopped looking for answers, and we never will. This is about justice, and it's about holding the person responsible accountable for what he did. We need the truth, no matter where it leads us, and we are not going to stop until we get it.

We worry about that every single day. But for us, doing nothing is much worse than the risk of false hope. Not knowing and not fighting for the truth is a kind of torture that never stops. We didn't make this decision lightly, but we have a duty to our daughter to push every door open, to demand accountability, and to leave no stone unturned. If we just walk away, we are accepting silence, and we can't live with that. We need answers, and we believe this lawsuit is the only way left to finally get them.

We think about that every single day, but the greater risk is staying silent and letting whatever happened to our daughter be swept under the rug. We aren't just doing this to get our hopes up; we are doing this because we need accountability and we refuse to give up on her. Every step we take, no matter how painful, brings us closer to the truth, and living with uncertainty is far more agonizing than the fight to find out where she is and who is responsible.

Well, I think that's the absolute hardest part of any situation like this. When you're searching for answers and looking for accountability, you naturally want to write the script for how it's all going to end. You want the other side to step up and give you the exact words, the exact closure you've been dreaming of. But the reality is, the people or institutions involved often don't have it in them to say what you need them to say, or they have their own scripts. 

So when you file something like a lawsuit, you're rolling the dice on whether they will ever truly acknowledge what went wrong. You have to ask yourself if you're holding out for words they may simply be incapable of giving, and whether chasing that specific outcome is going to bring you peace or just keep the wound wide open.

The Saudis are going to push for a continuation, and perhaps even an intensification, of the maximum pressure campaign against Iran. They see Tehran as their primary regional rival, and they want Washington fully aligned with that view. But Secretary Pompeo needs to listen with a degree of caution. While Riyadh's concerns about Iranian regional activity are real, a purely escalatory approach risks stumbling into a wider military confrontation that neither the region nor the United States can afford. Rather than offering a blank check to Saudi Arabia's maximalist agenda, Washington should be using its leverage to encourage a diplomatic de-escalation between Riyadh and Tehran. The Saudis themselves have started testing the waters of direct dialogue with the Iranians because they recognize the limits of American protection and the dangers of unmanaged regional conflict. The Secretary should encourage that diplomatic track rather than undermining it.

I think what Secretary Pompeo will hear from the Saudis is a continuation of their deep-seated anxiety regarding Iran's regional influence and its nuclear ambitions. Riyadh and Abu Dhabi have always been maximalist in their approach, and they will likely push Washington to maintain or even escalate the maximum pressure campaign. 

How closely he should listen is a different question. While the United States certainly needs to coordinate with its regional partners, adopting the Saudi and Emirati agenda wholesale has proven to be a recipe for escalation without a diplomatic off-ramp. Instead of outsourcing U.S. policy to regional capitals that often want to fight Iran to the last American, Washington needs to pursue a balanced strategy that combines deterrence with a credible diplomatic horizon. If the U.S. simply echoes Riyadh's talking points, it risks getting dragged into a conflict that neither the American public nor the region can afford.

Well, I think the Secretary is going to hear the standard assurances and denials regarding the Khashoggi investigation, but he needs to look past the rhetoric and focus on the intelligence we already have. How closely should he listen? With a heavy dose of skepticism. The Saudis are vital strategic partners in the region, particularly regarding Iran, but our relationship cannot be built on blind trust or a willingness to look the other way when fundamental human rights and international norms are violated. He needs to deliver a very firm, unequivocal message that accountability is non-negotiable. At the same time, we have to maintain a channel of communication because stability in the Middle East requires it. It is a delicate diplomatic tightrope, but America's credibility on the global stage depends on standing by our values, not just our economic and security interests.

I think Secretary Pompeo will hear a familiar refrain from the Saudi leadership, which is an encouragement to maintain the maximum pressure campaign against Iran and perhaps even double down on it. The Saudis view everything through the prism of their regional rivalry with Tehran, so their advice will predictably lean toward confrontation. As for how closely he should listen, I would argue he needs to exercise a healthy degree of skepticism. While the alliance with Riyadh is important, hitching American foreign policy entirely to the parochial and often escalatory objectives of one regional partner is a recipe for disaster.
